nodes.question: How was the surface area and pore size distribution of the samples determined?
nodes.answer: The surface area and pore size distribution were determined by nitrogen adsorption/desorption isotherm using the Quantochrome Autosorp device.
nodes.paragraph: The surface morphology and composi- tion of the samples with were examined using SEM (JEOL JSM 5600) assisted by EDS. FTIR spectra (Bruker 22) of the samples were obtained at wavelengths of 500 4000 cm 1. Surface area and pore size distribution of the sample by nitrogen adsorption/desorption isotherm was determined Biomass Conversion and Biorefinery with the Quantochrome Autosorp device. For this purpose, the sample was degassed at 200 C for 3 h under vacuum (0.4 bar). The Brunauer Emmett Teller (BET) surface area value was determined in the relative pressure (P/PO) range from 0.1 to 0.99. However, the pore volume and distribu- tion were determined by the Barrett-Joyner-Halenda (BJH) method, 2 = 10 80 range. 2.3 Electrochemical tests A manually connected Nova 2.1.5 model Autolab (PGSTAT128N) device with a triple cell stand (BASi) was used for electrochemical experiments. The capacitor proper - ties of the electrode prepared from iodine@S-doped SPAC material were examined by GCD, EI,S and CV methods. For electrochemical analyses, 1 M H2SO4, 1 M NaOH, and 1 M Na2SO4 were used as electrolyte solutions.

nodes.question: How does micro-XCT differ from standard XCT?
nodes.answer: Micro-XCT provides sub-millimeter and even sub-micron XCT to examine the physical properties and morphological composition of samples, whereas standard XCT may not achieve this level of resolution.
nodes.paragraph: In XCT, a series of radiographs are collected as a function ofsample rotation and then are mathematically recon-structed to produce a three-dimensional (3D) dataset. 34ut BE ;t /C2 u0e/COR/C1t 1 As the name implies, laboratory-based XCT sys- items can be installed as a standalone system in a laboratory as opposed to using larger facilities such as synchrotron sources. Micro-XCT, which providessub-millimeter and even sub-micron XCT to exam- line samples physical properties and morphological composition, has become more available due toengineering and technological advances. Theseadvances 35 38include scintillator-coated micro- scopes and improvements in X-ray sources to reduce the X-ray spot size, both of which increase theachievable spatial resolution of the system. The introduction of micro-XCT as a routine capability in the PIE process has enabled XCT to provide deeperinsights into fundamental material science phenomena. The laboratory-based micro-XCT at IMCL is particularly useful for quantifying voids and cracks in samples, examining internal interfaces between different structures or materials within specimens, ,measuring surface roughness, and identifying post-test sample changes in regimes spanning from the engineering scale to the microscale. When inte- grated with other examination techniques, XCT canhelp enable correlative microscopy which can provide information on a sample from the engineer- ing length scale down to the atomic level.

nodes.question: What volume of filtered seawater was used in the incubation chambers for symbiont sampling?
nodes.answer: A volume of 150 mL of 0.2 m filtered seawater was used in the incubation chambers.
nodes.paragraph: Methods Coral collections Thirty-two colonies of the reef-building scleractinians Montastraea cavernosa (Mcav), Pseudodiploria clivosa (Pcli), Orbicella faveolata (Ofav), Siderastrea siderea (Ssid), Diploria labyrinthiformis (Dlab), and Acropora cervicornis (Acer) were opportunistically collected between December 2020 and February 2022 from salvage operations on reefs between Biscayne National Park and the Port of Miami in south Florida, USA (under permit SAL-22-2243C- SCRP). Between four and eight genets of each species (Mcav, n = 5; Pcli, n = 8; Ofav, n = 5; Ssid, n = 5, Dlab, n = 4; Acer, n = 4) were fragmented into 2.5-cm-diameter circular cores using a drill press or 5 cm2 ramets (A. cervicornis) and given ample time to heal (at least 2 weeks). This was done to prevent measuring loss of symbionts from tissue lesions. Two replicate fragments per genet were used throughout the experiment. Symbiont sampling Incubation chambers were pre-prepared with 150 mL of 0.2 m filtered seawater (FSW). This was done to ensure that symbionts observed in the seawater were due to expulsion rather than a product of free-living symbionts in the water source.

nodes.question: How was the pure Pb(NO3)2 solution obtained from the initial mixture?
nodes.answer: The pure Pb(NO3)2 solution was obtained by filtration through a 0.22 m filter.
nodes.paragraph: Briefly, REEs/C (0.5 g) and 15 mg L 1 Pb(NO3)2 solution (50 ml) were put into a 150 ml transparent glass conical flask together. Then, it was shaken at 30 C and 250 rpm for 90 min to ensure sufficient reaction between REEs/Cs and lead nitrate solution. Ultimately, a pure Pb(NO3)2 solution was obtained by filtration through a 0.22 m filter for analysis using Atomic Absorption Spectrometer (AAS, V ARIAN AA240, USA). The concentration of REEs in solution was analysed by Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS, X-Series 2, Thermo Scientific, Massachusetts, USA). Three replicates were set up for all treatments. The removal experiment of heavy metal in mine wastewater was designed to test the potential of REEs/C for practical applications. Briefly, REEs/C (0.1 g) was placed in a 150 ml clear glass conical flask along with actual wastewater (50 ml) from a mine in Fujian Province. Then, it was shaken at 30 C and 250 rpm to ensure sufficient reaction between REEs/Cs and lead nitrate solution.

nodes.question: What equipment was used for the peptide separation process?
nodes.answer: The peptide mixture was separated using a NanoACQUITY UPLC MClass system.
nodes.paragraph: Before peptide separation, the samples were dissolved in 20 L of 0.1% (v/v) formic acid and 2% (v/v) acetonitrile (ACN). The peptide mixture was separated by reversed-phase chromatography on a NanoACQUITY UPLC MClass system (Waters) with MassLynx V4.1 (Waters) software. For the digestion of proteins, 200 ng was injected into an ACQUITY UPLC M-Class C18 column (5 m, 180 m 20 mm, 100 A) and desalted under isocratic conditions at a flow rate of 15 L/min in 99% formic acid and 1% (v/v) ACN buffer for 3 min. The peptide mixture was subjected to reversed-phase chromatography on a C18 column (100 , 1.8 mm, 75 m 150 mm) PepMap column (Waters) for 130 min at 35 C at a flow rate of 300 nL/min using a two-part linear gradient from 1% (v/v) ACN, 0.1% formic acid to 35% (v/v) ACN, 0.1% formic acid and from 35% (v/v) ACN, 0.1% formic acid to 85% (v/v) ACN, 0.1% formic acid.

nodes.question: What particles predominantly pass through wet scrubbers and what is their size range?
nodes.answer: Particles in the size range of 60-200 nm predominantly pass through wet scrubbers, constituting a significant portion of the inhalable particle mass.
nodes.paragraph: In contrast to analyses of the aerosol S bulk composition, single-particle analysis is capable of revealing changes in the distribution of pollutants across the aerosol ensemble. This allows for a deeper understanding of the removal mechanisms in the scrubber and provides an estimate of the potential environ- mental and health effects of the remaining particles. Experimental A single-cylinder, four-stroke, 80-kW research ship engine with common rail injection was operated using heavy fuel oil with 2.4% (m/m) fuel sulfur content, and, for run-in and comparison, marine gas oil with 0.1% fuel sulfur content. With a large displacement of 3.18 L and the capability to run on all marine fuels, this engine is a well-established model for ship propulsion systems [30]. The two investigated loads of 60 kW (75%) and 20 kW (25%) are representa- tive of cruising and maneuvering conditions, respectively. Measurements began after a 20-min stabilization phase to avoid instabilities in the emissions that often occur during the start-up and warm-up phases. A downscaled research wet scrubber (SAACKE, Germany) with a total wash tower vol- ume of 0.9 m3 was specifically designed and adapted for the 80-kW research ship engine.
